HubSpot CRM
Sync donation data and supporter information between Fundraise Up and HubSpot.
HubSpot is a cloud-based Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platform that helps organizations improve communication with customers and automate business processes. It supports marketing, sales, service, and content management functions, making it a versatile tool for growing organizations. The Fundraise Up integration automatically sends donation data to HubSpot, so you don’t need to enter information manually or use third-party solutions.
How the integration works 
When supporters donate through Fundraise Up, the integration sends their information to HubSpot in real time. Each donation creates the corresponding records in your CRM.
Records appear in HubSpot before a payment succeeds. This happens with recurring plans, where an upcoming payment exists before it is charged, and with payment methods that take several days to clear, such as ACH, SEPA, and bank debit. The Deal stage reflects the state of the payment and updates as the payment moves between states.
The integration starts in a paused state when you connect your accounts, so you can configure mappings and settings before data transfers. After you enable sync, new donations generate records in HubSpot based on your configuration.
When a donation is received, the integration creates or updates records in HubSpot:
Deals: Individual donations with amounts, dates, and campaign details.
Contacts: Supporters with personal and contact information.
Subscriptions: Recurring donation plans with status, frequency, and payment details.
Companies: Organizations linked to donations made on behalf of an organization.
Deals 
The integration creates Deals in HubSpot to represent one-time donations and installments of recurring donations. All Deals are automatically placed in a dedicated "Fundraise Up Donations" pipeline that the integration creates in your HubSpot account at the time of connection.
The integration fills in the following fields by default:
Amount
Close Date (left empty until the payment clears)
Deal Name (based on your integration settings in Fundraise Up)
Deal Stage (set from the donation status — see Pipeline stages below)
Pipeline stages 
Every Deal sits in a stage of the Fundraise Up Donations pipeline. The stage comes from the donation status in Fundraise Up:
succeeded — the payment went through.
scheduled — an upcoming payment on a recurring plan that has not been charged yet. This also covers one-time donations scheduled for a later date.
pending — the funds are on their way but not yet confirmed. Donations paid by ACH, SEPA, or bank debit start here and move to succeeded once they clear.
retrying — a payment on a recurring plan did not go through, and Fundraise Up is retrying it.
refunded — the donation was refunded.
failed — the payment did not go through. This is most often a payment on a recurring plan.
By default, succeeded maps to success, refunded maps to refund, failed maps to failed, and scheduled, pending, and retrying all map to pending. Because three statuses share the pending stage, a Deal in that stage may be an upcoming recurring payment, a payment still clearing, or a payment in retries.
To change a mapping, open Pipeline stages and choose a different stage for the status.
Contacts 
For each donation, the integration attempts to find an existing Contact based on your "Match contact" setting configured in Fundraise Up (explained below).
If the integration finds a match, it links the Deal to that Contact and updates their information based on the supporter’s profile. If it doesn’t find a match, it creates a new Contact and associates the Deal with the new Contact.
The integration reads contact data from the supporter profile, not from personal information entered during a specific donation. If a supporter’s name or address changes at checkout, that change applies only to that donation record — it does not update the supporter profile and will not sync to HubSpot. To update a supporter’s profile, the change must be made through the supporter profile in the Fundraise Up Dashboard or through the Donor Portal.
When a match is found or a new Contact is created, the integration updates fields including:
Name
Email address
Email mailing list opt-in status
Phone number
Physical address
Subscriptions 
The integration syncs recurring donation data to the Subscriptions object. All Deals that represent donations from recurring plans in Fundraise Up are automatically linked to their corresponding Subscription record.
The integration fills in the following fields:
Amount
Created date
Currency
Frequency
ID
Payment method
Payment method type
Previous installment date
Status
Companies 
When a supporter donates on behalf of an organization, the integration links the donation to a Company in HubSpot.
The integration looks for an existing Company first by organization name, then by the supporter’s corporate email domain. A public email domain, such as gmail.com, is not used for matching. When the integration finds a match — or has enough detail to create one — it uses or creates the Company, then associates both the Contact and the Deal with it. When there is not enough detail to identify a Company, the integration creates none and instead passes the organization details for you to handle through a HubSpot workflow.
The organization name comes from the on behalf of field the supporter fills in at checkout, not from the Contact’s employer field.
A DAFpay donation works differently when you select Sync the sponsor fund (DAF) as the donor. The Company is the supporter’s sponsor fund rather than the organization they named at checkout, and that Company becomes the donor of the Deal. See “DAF donations” below.
Company matching requires additional HubSpot permissions that earlier connections did not grant. Reconnect the integration to grant them. Until you reconnect, the integration does not create or match Companies, and no other behavior changes.
Limitations 
Before using the integration, review the following known limitations:
Pipeline requirements. You must have at least one available pipeline in addition to the core HubSpot system pipeline. This means you need a minimum of two pipelines on your HubSpot plan, and at least one must be available.
HubSpot tier requirements. Fundraise Up cannot support HubSpot integration for organizations using only HubSpot Free tools. This tier is too limited to enable proper data transmission from Fundraise Up to HubSpot.
Currency validation. HubSpot requires valid currency codes. If supporters donate in currencies that are not enabled in your HubSpot account, you may see sync errors. See the Troubleshooting section for solutions. See Resolving currency validation errors in HubSpot integration.
Set up the integration 
Follow these steps to connect your Fundraise Up and HubSpot accounts to sync donation data between platforms.
Before you begin 
You’ll need:
Organization Administrator role in Fundraise Up (required to add integrations).
Administrator access in HubSpot.
At least one available pipeline in HubSpot (in addition to the core system pipeline).
Connect your HubSpot account 
Go to Settings > Integrations in your Fundraise Up Dashboard.
Click Add Integration and select HubSpot.
Click Connect HubSpot.
You’ll be redirected to HubSpot to authorize the connection.
Log in to HubSpot if you haven’t already in this browser.
Choose your HubSpot account to connect.
Click Connect app to authorize Fundraise Up to access your HubSpot data.
You can connect multiple HubSpot environments to a single Fundraise Up account. This is useful for organizations with multiple departments or for setting up sandbox testing environments.
Configure the integration settings 
Once connected, configure the integration from its page in the Dashboard. Start with the General settings tab.
General settings tab
Configure general settings 
General settings control basic sync behavior and set defaults for all donations. The only mandatory fields are Deal name (pre-filled) and Match contact (defaulting to "By email"), but we recommend reviewing all settings to ensure records are created in HubSpot exactly as you’d like.
Sync test data: Check this option if you want test mode donations to appear in HubSpot. Use this to verify that your mapping rules work correctly before processing live donations.
Subaccount sync: Only appears if your account has subaccounts. Choose whether no subaccounts, selected subaccounts, or all subaccounts send data to HubSpot through this integration. New integrations start with Don’t sync subaccounts. A subaccount that syncs can set its own mapping rules on top of yours.
Deal name: Controls the name format for Deal records created in HubSpot. This field is pre-filled with a recommended format but you can customize it.
Match contact: Controls how the integration identifies existing supporters in HubSpot. You can choose from four options:
By email (default): Matches supporters by email address only.
By email or name: Matches supporters if either the email or name matches.
By email or name and address: Matches supporters if either the email matches, or both name and physical address match.
By email or name and phone: Matches supporters if either the email matches, or both name and phone match.
Subscription type (optional): HubSpot uses subscription types to store what types of communication a contact has or has not consented to receive. This dropdown allows you to control which subscription type the integration updates on Contacts based on the supporter’s consent preferences during checkout.
Refund sync mode: Controls how refunded donation amounts sync to HubSpot. By default, when a donation is refunded, the Deal stage changes to Refunded and the Deal amount updates to a negative value reflecting the refunded payout. You can change this:
Sync default — keeps the default behavior described above.
Sync as zero — syncs the Deal amount as $0 instead.
Sync only status — changes the Deal stage to Refunded without updating the amount.
Changes you make aren’t saved until you click Save changes.
Soft credits 
A soft credit attributes a donation to someone who influenced it without being its donor of record. When a supporter donates through a peer-to-peer fundraiser’s page, the supporter who gave receives the hard credit, and the fundraiser who drove the donation receives the soft credit. Soft credits let your organization measure how much each fundraiser brings in. They do not affect financial totals. Donations through DAFpay can use soft credits differently — see “DAF donations” below.
Soft credits require HubSpot Professional or Enterprise, because they rely on association labels. On a lower tier the Sync soft credits checkbox still appears and can still be selected, but no soft credit is recorded: Fundraise Up links only the supporter to the Deal, without a label, and does not create a Contact for the fundraiser.
By default, Fundraise Up syncs the hard credit only. To also sync soft credits, select the Sync soft credits checkbox.
With soft credits turned on, each Deal that comes through a fundraiser’s page carries two Contacts: the supporter who paid, labeled Hard credit, and the fundraiser, labeled Soft credit. Fundraise Up creates both labels in your HubSpot account on the first sync. You can rename them in HubSpot without breaking the sync.
The soft credit covers the full Deal amount. An association label carries no amount of its own, so partial soft credits are not possible.
Fundraise Up looks for the fundraiser in HubSpot using the same Match contact setting it uses for supporters. When it finds no match, it creates a Contact with the fundraiser’s first name, last name, and email address.
Soft credits apply to one-time and recurring donations. Each installment of a recurring donation creates its own Deal carrying both labels.
When a donation is refunded, Fundraise Up unlinks the fundraiser from the Deal completely, whatever your Refund sync mode setting is. The supporter stays linked with the Hard credit label, and the Deal itself follows that setting as usual.
DAF donations 
A supporter who gives through DAFpay recommends a grant from a donor-advised fund. The sponsor fund that administers that account is the legal donor of the donation your organization receives. Many organizations record these donations with the sponsor fund as the donor and the supporter who recommended the grant as a soft credit.
By default, Fundraise Up records the supporter as the donor, the same as with any other payment method. To record the sponsor fund as the donor instead, select the Sync the sponsor fund (DAF) as the donor checkbox. It appears only when soft credits are available for this connection and your connection grants the HubSpot permissions needed to create Companies. If the checkbox is missing, reconnect the integration to grant those permissions.
With the checkbox selected, a DAFpay donation syncs like this:
The Deal is associated with a Company named after the sponsor fund, which makes that Company the donor. Fundraise Up matches the Company by exact name and creates it when none exists.
The supporter stays linked to the Deal as a Contact with the Soft credit label. Fundraise Up doesn’t apply the Hard credit label to the supporter.
The checkbox changes DAFpay donations only. Every other payment method continues to record the supporter as the donor.
Fundraise Up records which model a donation used the first time that donation syncs, and keeps it. Selecting the checkbox doesn’t change DAF donations that already synced, and clearing it doesn’t move donations already synced under the sponsor fund back to the supporter.
DAF Tracking ID and DAF External ID are available as Fundraise Up properties in your mapping rules. The checkbox doesn’t affect them.
Set up mapping rules 
Mapping rules connect fields in Fundraise Up to fields in HubSpot. Default mappings cover standard fields like donation amounts and dates, but you can add custom mappings to match your data structure.
Mapping rules tab
To add a mapping:
Go to the Mapping rules tab.
Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Add rule.
Select the Fundraise Up object (entity) and property (field) on the left.
Select the corresponding HubSpot entity and field on the right.
Click Save changes.
Fundraise Up entities to map data from:
Account
Campaign
Checkout question
Custom field
Designation
Donation
Recurring
Static value (this allows you to enter a specific value to pass for every donation)
UTM parameter
HubSpot entities to map data to:
Contact
Deal
Custom objects 
In HubSpot, custom objects are object types that your organization creates for data that standard objects, such as Contacts and Deals, don’t cover. When you map Fundraise Up data to a custom object, each donation or recurring plan creates or updates a record of that object.
Custom object mappings are configured on the Custom objects tab. They work alongside your mapping rules and do not replace them.
Available objects 
Custom objects require a HubSpot Enterprise plan.
The object list shows the custom objects in your HubSpot account. For each object, the field list shows the fields that the integration can write to.
A custom object can sync donations or recurring plans, but it can’t sync both. To sync both, use two custom objects.
Fundraise Up doesn’t associate custom object records with the supporter’s Contact or the donation’s Deal. You can find them in the record list of the custom object in HubSpot. They don’t appear on the Contact or Deal record.
Add a custom object 
To map Fundraise Up data to a custom object:
Go to the Custom objects tab.
Click Add custom object.
On the Fundraise Up side, choose an entity, then a field.
On the HubSpot side, choose an object, then a field.
Click Save changes.
The Fundraise Up side offers the same entities as your mapping rules, including static values. Add a rule for each field you want to sync.
Map every required field of the object. If a rule for a required field is missing, Fundraise Up doesn’t create the record.
Sync behavior 
Custom objects sync after the standard records and mapping rules. The first sync of a donation or recurring plan creates a record in the custom object, and later syncs update that record. If someone deletes the record in HubSpot, Fundraise Up creates it again on the next sync.
HubSpot accepts custom object records in groups. If one record in a group has invalid data, HubSpot rejects the whole group, so records for other donations in that group aren’t saved either.
An error in a custom object mapping doesn’t stop the standard sync. Deals, Contacts, and Subscriptions still sync as usual.
Sync your data 
After completing your setup, choose how you want data to sync — automatically for real-time updates or manually for more control over the process.
Sync settings 
Find sync controls at the bottom of your HubSpot integration page. These settings determine how and when data transfers to HubSpot.
Automatic sync 
By default, automatic sync is disabled when you first connect so you can configure settings before data transfers.
Click Enable automatic sync after you finalize your settings and mapping rules.
New donations sync to HubSpot in real time, including installments of recurring donation plans.
Manual sync 
Use manual sync when you need more control over when data transfers:
Sync specific date ranges or your entire donation history.
Update records in HubSpot after making changes in Fundraise Up.
Test your integration settings with controlled data transfers.
Make bulk corrections after updating mapping rules.
Click Start manual sync to begin. You can choose from these sync options:
Unsynced live donations: Includes donations with sync issues (such as failed attempts) and donations that haven’t been synchronized before.
All live donations: Synchronizes all live donations regardless of sync status. Use this to re-sync previously imported records or ensure all data is current.
All test donations: Synchronizes all test donations (only available if you have Sync test data enabled).
You can also select a date range for your sync. After you click Start sync, the process begins. Refresh the page and scroll down to see the progress and results.
Sync log and sync options
Sync log 
The sync log provides a record of sync activity and status for each attempt.
To access the sync log:
Scroll to the Synced donations section.
Review the history of sync attempts, their status, and any error messages.
Each entry shows:
When the sync occurred.
Which records were processed.
Success or failure status.
Button to resync individual records if needed.
If errors occur, the sync log provides details to help troubleshoot the issue.
Disconnect the integration 
You can disconnect HubSpot at any time. If you connect the same account again in the future, all your previous settings and mappings are preserved.
To disconnect:
Scroll to the bottom of the integration page.
Click Disconnect.
Disconnecting stops all data syncing. Reconnecting restores your previous settings, but past data won’t sync automatically.
Troubleshooting 
If you encounter issues with your HubSpot integration, here are resources that can help:
When supporters give in different currencies, you may see sync errors if those currencies aren’t enabled in your HubSpot account. Learn how to resolve currency validation errors.
HubSpot integration FAQ.
For other problems or questions, contact Fundraise Up support with your sync log details.
